title: Remarks at Newark, Ohio
paragraphs: I shall not attempt to make a set speech to you. I shall merely say what a pleasure it is to be greeted by you. I am to come back to Ohio. Now I am merely on my way down to the meeting of the Firemen's Association at Chattanooga. I have always been rather fond of the railroad men. I want to thank you for coming, and I know the rest of you won't grudge my saying that I wish to thank particularly the men of the great war, the veterans, for coming to greet me. Good luck go with you. (Cheers.)
